page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 35 MB of L3 cache along with support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. It does not feature local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard compute engines. Network connectivity is configured with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded applications, contrasting with weaker isolated single-core throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 11,934.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,894.0, while single-threaded tasks like stress-ng single-core execution and gzip compression land in the lower quartile of comparative tests. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 71.19 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 42.85 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, the server delivers 9.0 GB/sec of static web serving throughput and handles 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation provides qualitative resource efficiency for parallel execution pipelines where large memory footprints are unnecessary. Workloads that benefit from this balanced compute architecture include compilation tasks, batch data processing, distributed web serving, and containerized microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration supplies 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with two threads per core, combined with 24.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and AES instructions, the instance contains no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core processing throughput, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,894.0 and 10.16 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core execution shows modest throughput. This profile suits multi-threaded batch workloads, backend web clusters, and general compilation tasks.
